text:
Barrett Hayton might be the most underrated part of Utah's season. The Mammoth get 63.7% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, more than ten points better than without him, and 56.4% of the shot attempts. Few forwards on any team can claim that kind of share.

The points don't reflect it. He has 13 in 26 games, 4 goals on 5.9 expected, shooting 7.8% against a league rate of 13.5%. Utah has also scored 3.9 fewer goals than expected with him on. Over his last ten he has 4 points against 5.2 expected. When a player drives play this well and finishes this poorly, it's usually the finishing that moves.

Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away last season (0.12 fewer expected goals against per 60 with him out there, 89th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 1.5 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net. The fifth overall pick from 2018 has become a two-way centre. For a Utah team losing close games, those chances need to start going in.
headline: Hayton's line is winning; the scoreboard hasn't noticed
